Accountable obligation owner.value: Controller owns the statutory ICFR risk-and-control matrix and drafts Management's Report of Internal Control over Financial Reporting; the Chief Financial Officer signs it and escalations on scope go to the Audit Committee

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Alaska AS 21.09.200 and 3 AAC 21 (Alaska's adoption of NAIC Model 205, Sections 15-16) re-read at each annual scoping; the Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona adoptions are diffed line-by-line against the current NAIC Model 205 text and the 51-jurisdiction adoption chart is refreshed each January

In-scope processes.value: The statutory close for every writing company whose prior-year direct plus assumed written premium exceeds the Section 16 $500 million threshold: premium and underwriting, claims and loss/LAE reserving, ceded and assumed reinsurance, invested assets and investment income, cash and treasury, taxes, and the Annual Statement compilation (Pages 2-5, Schedule P, Schedule F, Schedule D)

In-scope systems.value: Statutory GL and its feeders (policy administration, claims platform, reinsurance administration, investment accounting) plus the NAIC Annual Statement compiler; the control matrix, narratives and owner attestations live in AuditBoard

Compliance procedure documented.value: Statutory ICFR Documentation Standard — annual scoping memo (premium threshold test, entity and account materiality), process narratives and flowcharts, risk-and-control matrix keyed to statutory account balance and assertion, control-owner attestation form, and the deficiency severity rubric (deficiency / significant deficiency / material weakness)

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved in writing by the Chief Financial Officer and accepted by the Audit Committee at its first-quarter meeting; re-approved annually and whenever a state amends its Model 205 adoption or the Section 16 premium threshold test changes result

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Matrix frozen for the reporting year at December 31; control-owner attestations due April 30; Management's Report of ICFR due August 1 — within 60 days of the June 1 audited statutory report filing — in every jurisdiction that adopted Section 16

Deadline reminders configured.value: Statutory close calendar milestones at Sep 30 (scoping refresh), Dec 31 (matrix freeze), Apr 30 (owner attestation), Jul 1 (Section 16 report draft to CFO), each firing owner reminders at 15 and 5 days out and an escalation to the Controller on the due date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Dated matrix versions, narratives, walkthrough memos, SOC 1 reports, owner attestations and the signed Management's Report of ICFR retained 7 years from the reporting year end in the compliance evidence repository, indexed by writing company and statutory year

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any key control without a named owner, evidence source or tested attribute is logged as an ICFR deficiency with severity grade, root cause, owner and remediation date, and carried to the next quarter until closed

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CFO signs closure of every material weakness and significant deficiency; the Controller signs lower-severity closures and reports them to the Audit Committee in the quarterly ICFR summary

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every key control in the frozen ICFR matrix for the reporting year across the in-scope writing companies, plus every December 31 trial balance account that rolls into a material Annual Statement line, exhibit or schedule

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Every material statutory account balance and relevant assertion must map to at least one key control with a named owner and a stated evidence source; any unmapped material balance is a fail, and any material weakness open at December 31 forces an adverse Section 16 conclusion

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is continuous; matrix completeness is re-validated against the GL trial balance quarterly and in full at the December 31 freeze before the annual Section 16 conclusion is drafted

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: The Chief Audit Executive and Internal Audit staff, none of whom authored the matrix, own a scoped control or perform any statutory close activity

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual ICFR scoping and coverage workpaper — trial balance to matrix mapping, coverage gap list, SOC 1 and CUEC assessment, conclusion memo — filed in AuditBoard and mirrored to the compliance evidence repository under the statutory year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Management's Report of ICFR, the risk-and-control matrix, process narratives, SOC 1 reports and the deficiency log, producible to a Division of Insurance financial condition examination team within 5 business days of an information request

Regulator response path.value: The Statutory Reporting Manager owns responses to Alaska Division of Insurance and lead-state financial analyst inquiries; General Counsel clears any written disclosure of a material weakness before it leaves the company

checklist.step: Run the Section 16 premium threshold test per writing company
actions: Open the prior-year filed Annual Statement for each writing company and read direct written premium from the State Page (Exhibit of Premiums and Losses, Column 1 grand total) and assumed premium from Schedule F Part 1.
Add direct plus assumed written premium per company and compare to the Model 205 Section 16 threshold of $500 million; record the computed figure, not just the yes/no.
Apply the Section 4 audit exemption test separately (under $1 million direct plus assumed premium and fewer than 1,000 policyholders/certificate holders) and note any company that qualifies.
Ask the Chief Financial Officer to confirm the group's insurance holding company structure so premium is aggregated the way the domiciliary state requires.
Record each company's conclusion on the annual ICFR scoping memo with the source page reference.
checklist.done: each writing company has a computed direct-plus-assumed premium figure, a Section 16 in-scope/out-of-scope conclusion and a cited source page.

checklist.step: Refresh the 51-jurisdiction Model 205 adoption matrix
actions: Pull the current NAIC Model 205 text and the NAIC adoption chart, then open each licensed state's insurance code section adopting the Annual Financial Reporting Model Regulation (rep: Alaska AS 21.09.200 and 3 AAC 21).

For each of the 51 jurisdictions record: audited report due date (June 1 baseline), whether Sections 15-16 (ICFR) were adopted, any raised or lowered premium threshold, and any state-specific audit committee provision.
Diff Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona against the NAIC model text and flag any wording that changes the company's obligation.
Send the diff summary to Regulatory Counsel for confirmation and store the reply against the matrix row.
Publish the refreshed matrix to the Controller and the Statutory Reporting Manager by January 31.
checklist.done: the matrix carries a due date, an ICFR-adoption flag, a threshold and a citation for all 51 jurisdictions, with counsel's confirmation attached.

checklist.step: Scope statutory accounts from the December trial balance
actions: Export the statutory-basis trial balance by legal entity from the GL as of September 30 for scoping and again at December 31 for the freeze.
Set entity and account materiality off statutory capital and surplus and document the percentage used and who approved it.

Mark in scope every account above materiality plus the qualitatively significant ones regardless of size: loss and LAE reserves, reinsurance recoverable, premium receivable and non-admitted balances, deferred tax, and invested assets carried at other than amortized cost.
Map each in-scope account to the Annual Statement line, exhibit or schedule it feeds (Page 3 line, Schedule P Part, Schedule F Part, Schedule D Part).
Hand the scoped account list to the Controls Analyst and file it as the scoping appendix.
checklist.done: the scoping appendix lists every in-scope account with its materiality basis and the Annual Statement line it supports.

checklist.step: Map scoped accounts to processes and name a process owner for each
actions: In AuditBoard open the ICFR scope module and create the process register: underwriting and premium, claims and reserving, ceded/assumed reinsurance, investments, treasury, tax, payroll, and financial close and reporting.
Attach each scoped account to exactly one primary process and record any secondary process that also touches it.
Name a process owner at director level or above for each process and confirm the name with that person's manager by email.
Record for each process the source systems it depends on (policy administration, claims platform, reinsurance administration, investment accounting, GL).
Flag any account with no owner as an open scoping item for the Controller.
checklist.done: every scoped account sits under a named process with a confirmed process owner and a listed source system.

checklist.step: Write or refresh the process narrative and flowchart for each in-scope process
actions: Sit with the process owner and walk the transaction from initiation to the GL entry to the Annual Statement line, capturing systems, hand-offs, approval points and reports used.
Write the narrative to name the what-could-go-wrong at each assertion (existence, completeness, valuation, rights and obligations, presentation) for the accounts the process touches.
Draw the flowchart with swim lanes per role and mark each control point with its control id from the matrix.
Have the process owner sign the narrative as accurate and date it; unsigned narratives do not enter the matrix.
Store the signed narrative and flowchart in the ICFR SharePoint library under <entity>/<statutory year>/<process>.
checklist.done: every in-scope process has a signed, dated narrative and flowchart naming the risks at assertion level.

checklist.step: Identify key controls and complete every matrix attribute
actions: For each what-could-go-wrong in the narrative, select the control that would catch a material misstatement and mark it KEY; leave the rest as secondary.

Complete on every key control row: control id, description, owner, frequency (per transaction / daily / monthly / quarterly / annual), type (preventive or detective, manual or automated), assertion(s) covered, evidence artifact and where it is stored.
Record the precision of each review control — the threshold or expectation the reviewer applies and what they do when it is breached — because a review with no stated precision cannot be tested.
List for each control the information produced by the entity (IPE) it relies on, naming the report, the system it comes from and its parameters.
Reject any key control whose evidence is 'reviewed in a meeting' with no artifact and send it back to the process owner for redesign.
checklist.done: no key control row has a blank attribute, and every review control states its precision and its IPE source.

checklist.step: Scope the IT general controls the key controls depend on
actions: List every application that produces an automated control or an IPE report for a key control: GL, policy administration, claims platform, reinsurance administration, investment accounting, the close tool and the Annual Statement compiler.

For each application scope ITGCs across access to programs and data (provisioning, de-provisioning, periodic user access review, privileged access), change management, and computer operations (job scheduling, backup and restore).
Confirm with the Head of IT who owns each ITGC and where the evidence sits (SailPoint access review campaign, change tickets, job monitoring logs).
Add each ITGC to the matrix linked to the business controls that depend on it, so an ITGC failure visibly taints those controls.
Note any application whose ITGCs are provided by a vendor and hand it to the Third-Party Risk Manager for SOC 1 coverage.
checklist.done: every financially relevant application has scoped ITGCs, a named owner and a link to the business controls relying on it.

checklist.step: Obtain and evaluate SOC 1 Type 2 reports from service organizations
actions: List service organizations touching statutory reporting: TPA claims administration, investment custodian and accounting agent, actuarial modelling bureau, payroll provider, and any policy administration SaaS host.

Request the current SSAE 18 SOC 1 Type 2 report from each vendor's relationship manager and check the report period covers the statutory year; where it stops short, obtain a bridge letter covering the gap to December 31.
Read Section IV for exceptions noted by the service auditor and record each exception, the vendor's response and whether it touches an account you scoped.
Confirm the report is Type 2 (operating effectiveness), not Type 1; a Type 1 provides no operating-effectiveness reliance and must be replaced by direct testing.
File each report and bridge letter in the compliance evidence repository and record the receipt date on the vendor's matrix row.
checklist.done: each in-scope service organization has a period-covering SOC 1 Type 2 (plus bridge letter) on file with its exceptions assessed.

checklist.step: Map complementary user entity controls into the matrix
actions: Extract the complementary user entity controls (CUECs) listed in each SOC 1 report — typically authorising users, reviewing vendor output reports, and reconciling vendor data to the GL.
For each CUEC identify the internal control that discharges it and record the mapping on the matrix; where none exists, raise a control gap to the process owner with a build date.
Confirm the reconciliation CUECs name the specific vendor report and the GL account they are reconciled to.
Tell the Chief Audit Executive which CUECs are new this year so they enter the test plan.
checklist.done: every CUEC in every SOC 1 report is either mapped to an internal control or logged as a gap with a build date.

checklist.step: Set the entity-level and fraud-risk controls
actions: Document the entity-level controls the statutory conclusion leans on: Audit Committee oversight cadence, code of conduct attestation, whistleblower hotline intake and disposition, delegation of authority, and the management review of reserve and investment valuation assumptions.

Run the annual fraud risk assessment with the Chief Financial Officer and the Chief Risk Officer covering management override of controls, reserve manipulation, and improper reinsurance risk transfer accounting.
For each fraud risk record the specific mitigating control — journal entry review of manual and top-side entries, actuarial reserve peer review, reinsurance risk transfer testing — with its owner.
Load these controls into the matrix tagged ENTITY-LEVEL or FRAUD so they cannot be de-scoped by an account materiality change.
checklist.done: entity-level and fraud-risk controls are documented, mapped to named fraud risks and tagged in the matrix.

checklist.step: Capture control-owner attestations for the reporting year
actions: Launch the AuditBoard attestation campaign to every key control owner by April 15 with a April 30 due date.

Require the owner to confirm in the form: the control description still matches what is performed, the frequency is accurate, the named evidence is retained and retrievable, and no failure occurred that was not reported.
Chase non-responders at day 7 and day 12 and escalate anyone still open at the due date to their process owner and the Chief Financial Officer.
Where an owner reports a change, route it through the matrix change-control step before the attestation is accepted.
Export the completed campaign as a PDF and file it as the attestation evidence for the year.
checklist.done: every key control has a completed, dated owner attestation and every reported change has been routed to change control.

checklist.step: Run change control over the matrix during the year
actions: Require a change request for any addition, removal, re-owner or re-scope of a key control, stating the business trigger (system release, reorganisation, new reinsurance treaty, new product line).
Assess each request for impact on assertion coverage and on the Internal Audit test plan, and notify the Chief Audit Executive where testing must be re-cut.
Have the Controller approve every removal of a key control in writing — removals are where coverage silently disappears.
Version the matrix on each approved change and keep the prior version immutable so the December 31 freeze can be reconstructed.
Reject undocumented edits and restore the prior version.
checklist.done: the matrix change log shows a trigger, an impact assessment and an approver for every change, with prior versions preserved.

checklist.step: Evaluate identified control deficiencies and assign a severity grade
actions: Take every deficiency raised by Internal Audit, by control owners and by the CPA's audit and enter it on the deficiency log with the account and assertion it affects.

Apply the rubric: estimate the maximum potential statutory misstatement, judge the likelihood of it not being prevented or detected, and grade DEFICIENCY, SIGNIFICANT DEFICIENCY or MATERIAL WEAKNESS against capital and surplus.
Aggregate related deficiencies affecting the same account or assertion before grading — three individually small reserve-process deficiencies can aggregate to a significant deficiency.
Record for each item the compensating control considered and why it does or does not reduce the grade.
Present the graded log to the Chief Financial Officer and the Audit Committee at the quarterly ICFR review.
checklist.done: every deficiency carries an account, an assertion, a graded severity with rationale, and an aggregation assessment.

checklist.step: Draft and sign Management's Report of Internal Control over Financial Reporting
actions: Draft the Section 16 report on company letterhead stating: management's responsibility for establishing and maintaining ICFR, the control framework used (COSO 2013), the statutory basis of the financial statements, and management's assessment as of December 31.

State the conclusion — effective, or not effective with each unremediated material weakness described — and confirm the report includes the statement that it covers internal control over statutory financial reporting.
Have the Controller tie every assertion in the report back to the frozen matrix, the attestation campaign and the deficiency log before signature.
Sign the report and have the Chief Executive Officer countersign where the domiciliary state requires it.
Save the signed PDF to the financial reporting repository and hand it to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for the August 1 filing.
checklist.done: a signed Section 16 report exists naming COSO 2013, the December 31 assessment date and a stated conclusion supported by the matrix.

checklist.step: Freeze, index and retain the ICFR evidence pack
actions: At December 31 lock the matrix version and copy the full pack — scoping memo, narratives and flowcharts, matrix export, SOC 1 reports and bridge letters, attestations, deficiency log, signed Section 16 report — into the compliance evidence repository.
Index the pack by writing company, statutory year, process and control id so an examiner request can be answered by control id.
Apply the 7-year retention label measured from the statutory year end and set the repository to block deletion before that date.
Run a retrieval test: pick five control ids at random and confirm the evidence opens from the index in under two minutes.
checklist.done: the frozen pack is filed, indexed by control id, labelled for 7-year retention and proven retrievable by a spot test.

testing.step: Build the population of statutory balances and key controls for the reporting year
actions: Extract the December 31 statutory trial balance by legal entity from the GL and the frozen key control export from AuditBoard on the same date.
Build one population row per material trial balance account showing its Annual Statement line and the key control ids mapped to it.
Add every entity-level, fraud and ITGC control as separate population rows so they cannot be lost in an account-driven view.
Have the extractor sign the population as complete and record the extraction timestamp and report parameters.
testing.done: the population is a signed, timestamped list of material accounts and every key control mapped to them.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the filed Annual Statement
actions: Tie the trial balance totals in the population to Page 2 (Assets), Page 3 (Liabilities, Surplus and Other Funds) and Page 4 (Statement of Income) of the filed Annual Statement, entity by entity.
Investigate every difference and classify it as a legitimate statutory reclassification, a non-admitted asset adjustment, or an unexplained difference.
Confirm each material Annual Statement line has at least one mapped key control; list lines with zero coverage as scoping exceptions.
Resolve or escalate every unexplained difference to the Controller before drawing the sample.
testing.done: the population reconciles to Pages 2-4 of the filed Annual Statement with every difference explained or escalated.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of key controls for coverage re-performance
actions: Take 100% of entity-level, fraud-risk and reserve/reinsurance valuation controls.
Take a seeded random sample of 40 remaining key controls stratified across processes so no process contributes more than a quarter of the sample.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Add every control changed during the year through matrix change control as a mandatory sample row.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from a recorded seed and covers all entity-level, fraud, valuation and changed controls.

testing.step: Re-perform the risk-to-control mapping without reading the matrix conclusion first
actions: For each sampled process read the signed narrative, list the what-could-go-wrongs by assertion yourself, and only then open the matrix.
Compare your list to the matrix: a risk you identified that has no key control is a coverage exception, and a matrix control covering no identified risk is an over-scoping observation.
Confirm the control description in the matrix matches what the narrative says is actually performed, including who performs it.
Capture your independent risk list into the workpaper as the basis for the comparison.
testing.done: each sampled process has an independent risk list and a documented comparison to the matrix coverage.

testing.step: Verify evidence and IPE integrity for each sampled control
actions: Request the named evidence artifact for one occurrence of each sampled control and confirm it exists, is dated inside the control period and shows the performer.
For every IPE report relied on, re-run the report from the source system with the recorded parameters and agree row counts and totals to the copy the control owner used.
Where an IPE cannot be reproduced, treat the dependent control as untestable and grade it a deficiency rather than a documentation issue.
Note any review control whose evidence is a signature with no visible review threshold applied.
testing.done: each sampled control has a dated evidence artifact and every relied-on IPE has been independently reproduced.

testing.step: Test the SOC 1 reliance and the CUEC mapping
actions: For each in-scope service organization confirm a SOC 1 Type 2 is on file, that its period plus any bridge letter covers January 1 to December 31, and that the opinion is unqualified.
Read the Section IV exceptions and confirm each one affecting a scoped account has a documented management response and, where needed, compensating internal testing.
Trace each CUEC listed in the report to an internal control in the matrix and test one occurrence of the reconciliation CUECs against the vendor report and the GL account.
List unmapped CUECs and uncovered period gaps as exceptions.
testing.done: every SOC 1 covers the full statutory year and every CUEC traces to a tested internal control or an exception.

testing.step: Recompute the Section 16 threshold and the materiality maths
actions: Recompute direct plus assumed written premium per writing company from the Annual Statement State Page and Schedule F Part 1 and compare to the $500 million Section 16 threshold recorded in the scoping memo.
Recompute entity and account materiality from statutory capital and surplus using the documented percentage and compare the resulting in-scope account list to the one used.
Recompute the June 1 filing date and the August 1 Section 16 date (60 days after the audited report filing) against each jurisdiction's adoption row.
Any account that should have been in scope under recomputed materiality but was excluded is an exception regardless of whether a control failed.
testing.done: the premium threshold, materiality and both statutory dates are independently recomputed and agree with the scoping memo.

testing.step: Test the attestation campaign and matrix change control for completeness
actions: Compare the attestation campaign recipient list to the frozen key control owner list and identify any control whose owner never attested.
Pull the matrix change log and confirm every removal of a key control carries a written Controller approval and an impact assessment.
Select five changes and confirm the prior matrix version is retrievable and that the December 31 freeze can be reconstructed from it.
Confirm each owner-reported change during attestation actually flowed into a change request.
testing.done: every key control has an owner attestation and every matrix change has an approver, an impact assessment and a preserved prior version.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracked issue per exception naming the control id or account, what was missing and which statutory assertion it touches.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — scoping missed the account, narrative stale after a system release, owner vacancy, IPE not reproducible, SOC 1 gap — and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date that lands before the December 31 matrix freeze so the Section 16 conclusion is not held hostage to an open item.
Feed any exception graded significant deficiency or above into the Controller's deficiency log for severity evaluation the same week.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a pre-freeze remediation date and, where severe, a deficiency log entry.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the Audit Committee
actions: Compute the coverage exception rate (material accounts with no key control divided by material accounts) and compare it to the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion — ICFR documentation effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind each element.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored no part of the matrix and owns no scoped control, sign the workpaper with name and date.
Table the conclusion and the open exception list at the next Audit Committee meeting through the board portal and record the minute reference in the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states a conclusion, a coverage exception rate and the Audit Committee minute reference where it was reported.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Chief Audit Executive owns the annual MAR key control test plan and its results; functional reporting to the Audit Committee, administrative to the Chief Executive Officer

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — NAIC Model 205 Sections 11 (communication of internal control related matters noted in an audit), 12 (report on significant deficiencies) and 16, as adopted by Alaska (AS 21.09.200 / 3 AAC 21) and confirmed against the Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona adoptions before each annual test plan is approved

In-scope processes.value: Testing of every key control in the frozen ICFR matrix — underwriting and premium, claims and loss/LAE reserving, ceded and assumed reinsurance, investments, treasury, tax, financial close and Annual Statement compilation — plus the ITGCs those controls depend on, for each Section 16 in-scope writing company

In-scope systems.value: Test plan, sampling, workpapers, exceptions and remediation tracking in AuditBoard, with evidence drawn from the statutory GL, BlackLine reconciliations, the policy and claims platforms and the SailPoint access review campaigns

Compliance procedure documented.value: MAR Control Testing Methodology — risk-ranking of key controls, sample size table by control frequency, walkthrough and re-performance standards, IPE validation rules, exception grading rubric and the remediation retest protocol

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Audit Committee when it approves the annual internal audit plan (typically the Q4 meeting for the following year), and re-approved on any mid-year scope change exceeding 10% of planned control tests

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Interim testing complete by September 30, roll-forward testing complete by January 31, remediation retest complete by February 28, findings reconciled to the CPA's Section 11 communication which the insurer must file within 60 days of the June 1 audited report (August 1); any unremediated significant deficiency report follows within 90 days

Deadline reminders configured.value: AuditBoard test milestones with automated reminders to each auditor at 10 and 3 days before the interim, roll-forward and retest cut-offs, plus a weekly open-exception digest to control owners from November through February

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Test programs, samples with selection seeds, re-performance workpapers, evidence copies, exception forms and retest results retained 7 years from the statutory year end in AuditBoard with a mirrored export in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Each failed control attribute is logged as a test exception with the sampled item id, the attribute failed, the graded severity, root cause, control owner, remediation action and retest date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Controller signs each remediation as designed and implemented; the Chief Audit Executive signs the retest result, and no deficiency closes on management assertion alone

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All key controls in the frozen ICFR matrix for the statutory year, with per-control populations drawn from the GL, the reconciliation tool, the policy and claims platforms and the access/change management systems for the control's operating period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero deviations tolerated on annual and quarterly controls; for higher-frequency controls a deviation triggers an extended sample of double the original size, and a second deviation fails the control outright; any control failing after extension is graded and cannot be de-scoped

checklist.step: Build the annual MAR control test plan from the frozen matrix
actions: Import the current key control export from the ICFR matrix into the AuditBoard testing module and reject any control missing a frequency, evidence source or owner — untestable rows go back to the Controller.
Risk-rank each control HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW using the account's materiality, the assertion covered, whether it is a management review control and whether it failed in the prior year.
Set the timing per control: interim testing through September 30 with a roll-forward to December 31, or single testing after year end for annual controls such as the reserve certification review.
Assign a named auditor and budgeted hours per control and confirm no auditor is assigned a control in a process they previously worked in.
Take the plan to the Audit Committee for approval alongside the annual internal audit plan and record the approval date.
checklist.done: every key control has a risk rank, a timing, a named auditor and Audit Committee approval of the plan.

checklist.step: Agree scope and reliance with the external CPA firm
actions: Meet the engagement partner and senior manager before interim fieldwork and exchange the key control list, showing which controls each side will test.
Agree the controls where the CPA intends to rely on internal audit work and confirm the documentation standard and reviewer sign-off they need to place reliance.
Agree the exception grading language so a deficiency called by either side reads the same way in the Section 11 communication.
Confirm the date the CPA needs internal audit results delivered so their fieldwork supports a June 1 audited report.
Minute the agreement and circulate it to the Controller and the Audit Committee chair.
checklist.done: a minuted scope and reliance agreement exists naming which controls each side tests and the delivery date for internal audit results.

checklist.step: Set the sample size for every control by frequency and risk
actions: Apply the methodology sample table: annual control 1, quarterly 2, monthly 2-5, weekly 5-15, daily 20-40, many-times-per-day 25-60, with the upper end used for HIGH risk-ranked controls.
For automated controls test one instance plus the supporting ITGCs rather than a statistical sample, and document that reasoning on the test program.
Define the population source per control — the exact report, system and parameters that produce the list of occurrences — and record it before selection.
Select the sample with a documented random seed and record the seed, population size and selection date so the selection can be re-drawn.
Have the Chief Audit Executive approve any sample size below the table minimum in writing.
checklist.done: every control has a defined population source, a table-compliant sample size and a recorded selection seed.

checklist.step: Perform walkthroughs to confirm the control is designed as documented
actions: Take one transaction per in-scope process from initiation through to the GL entry and the Annual Statement line, observing each control point with the person who performs it.
Ask the performer to demonstrate the control on a live item rather than describe it, and note where practice diverges from the narrative.
Confirm the reviewer of each management review control can state the threshold they apply and show a case where they challenged an item.
Update the narrative through the Controls Analyst where practice has drifted, and log a design deficiency where the drift means the risk is no longer covered.
Write the walkthrough memo naming the transaction id, the date, the people met and the conclusion on design.
checklist.done: each in-scope process has a dated walkthrough memo citing a real transaction and a stated conclusion on control design.

checklist.step: Test design effectiveness against the assertion the control claims to cover
actions: For each sampled control ask whether, operating as described, it would prevent or detect a material misstatement of the assertion it is mapped to.
Check the precision: a monthly review of a variance report with a $5 million threshold cannot cover a $1 million materiality — record the threshold and the materiality side by side.
Confirm segregation of duties where the control depends on it, by comparing the performer and the preparer against the system role assignment.
Grade design as effective or not effective and write the reasoning; a not-effective design ends the test — do not proceed to operating effectiveness.
checklist.done: each sampled control has a documented design conclusion with its precision threshold compared to materiality.

checklist.step: Test operating effectiveness of manual controls
actions: Request the evidence for each selected occurrence directly from the control owner with a 5-business-day response window and record late responses.

Test the defined attributes on each item: performed by the authorised person, performed within the required timeframe, exceptions identified, exceptions investigated and resolved, and evidence of the resolution.
For review controls obtain the underlying data the reviewer looked at, not just the signed cover, and confirm items breaching the threshold were actually followed up.
Record a pass or a deviation per attribute per item — never a blanket pass for a sample.
On the first deviation extend the sample to double the original size and re-test before concluding.
checklist.done: every sampled occurrence has an attribute-level result and any deviation triggered a documented extended sample.

checklist.step: Test automated application controls and validate the IPE behind them
actions: For each automated control obtain the configuration screenshot showing the rule, tolerance or edit check as configured in the GL, policy administration or claims platform.
Process a test item through the control or inspect a rejected item to prove the rule fires, and record the item id and the date.
Confirm through the change management record that the configuration has not changed since the last test, or re-test from the change date.
Re-run every relied-on report from the source system with the recorded parameters and agree totals and row counts to the copy the control owner used; treat unreproducible IPE as a control failure.
checklist.done: each automated control has configuration evidence, a proven firing instance, a change-history check and reproduced IPE.

checklist.step: Test the ITGCs supporting the financially relevant applications
actions: Access: pull the current user list per application from SailPoint, sample new joiners, leavers and privileged accounts, and confirm approved provisioning, same-day de-provisioning for leavers, and a completed periodic access review with remediation of flagged access.
Change: sample production changes from the change tickets, confirm each has a business approval, evidence of testing in a non-production environment, and a separate deployer from the developer.
Operations: sample scheduled financial jobs and confirm failures were detected and rerun, and test one restore from backup for the GL.
Where an ITGC fails, mark every dependent business control as reliant on a failed ITGC and re-assess whether it can still be relied on.
checklist.done: access, change and operations ITGCs are tested per application and every failure is propagated to the dependent business controls.

checklist.step: Test the close, reconciliation and journal entry controls
actions: Sample balance sheet reconciliations from the close tool for the in-scope statutory accounts and confirm each was prepared, independently reviewed and certified within the close calendar deadline.
Confirm reconciling items are aged, explained and cleared, and that any item older than 90 days has a documented action owner.
Sample manual and top-side journal entries above the review threshold and confirm each has support attached and an approver different from the preparer.
Test the completeness of the journal population by agreeing the entry count and net value in the sample source to the GL journal register for the period.
checklist.done: sampled reconciliations are certified on time with aged items owned, and sampled journals have segregated approval and attached support.

checklist.step: Evaluate every exception and grade its severity
actions: For each exception record the control id, sampled item, attribute failed, the deviation rate over the sample and the account and assertion affected.
Estimate the maximum potential misstatement the failure exposes and compare it to statutory materiality and to capital and surplus.
Grade DEFICIENCY, SIGNIFICANT DEFICIENCY or MATERIAL WEAKNESS and document the compensating control considered and why it does or does not mitigate.
Have the control owner confirm the factual accuracy of the exception in writing before it is graded — dispute the facts, not the grade.
Escalate any provisional material weakness to the Chief Financial Officer and the Audit Committee chair within 2 business days of grading.
checklist.done: every exception carries a deviation rate, a maximum potential misstatement, a documented grade and owner-confirmed facts.

checklist.step: Aggregate deficiencies across accounts and processes
actions: Group all open deficiencies by statutory account and by assertion, including those raised by the external CPA and by control owners themselves.
Assess whether individually minor deficiencies affecting the same account or assertion aggregate to a significant deficiency or material weakness, and document the aggregation reasoning.
Assess pervasive causes — a failed access ITGC, a stale narrative after a system release, an unfilled control owner role — that touch multiple processes at once.
Present the aggregated view to the Controller and the Chief Audit Executive before any individual grade is finalised.
checklist.done: a written aggregation assessment exists by account and by assertion, covering internal and CPA-raised deficiencies together.

checklist.step: Agree remediation plans with the control owners
actions: For each graded deficiency agree with the control owner the specific change — redesign the control, add evidence capture, reassign the performer, fix the access rule, automate the reconciliation — not a promise to be more careful.
Set an implementation date that leaves at least 30 days of operation before December 31 so the control can be retested in the same statutory year.
Name the accountable owner and the executive sponsor, and record the interim mitigating action covering the period until the fix lands.
Reject remediation plans whose only action is additional training where the underlying design is the cause.
checklist.done: every graded deficiency has a specific remediation action, a named owner, an interim mitigation and a date allowing 30 days of operation before year end.

checklist.step: Retest remediated controls before the year-end conclusion
actions: Confirm the remediation was actually implemented by inspecting the changed procedure, configuration or role assignment and recording the go-live date.
Draw a fresh sample covering only occurrences after the go-live date, sized to the control frequency, and test the same attributes as the original test.

Where the post-remediation operating period is too short for the table sample, state that explicitly and carry the deficiency as unremediated at December 31 rather than concluding on insufficient evidence.
Have the second reviewer sign the retest workpaper before the deficiency is closed.
checklist.done: each remediated control has an implementation date, a post-go-live sample and a reviewer-signed retest conclusion or an explicit carry-forward.

checklist.step: Reconcile internal audit findings to the CPA's Section 11 communication
actions: Obtain from the engagement partner the written communication of internal control related matters noted in the audit (the management letter) which the insurer must file with the domiciliary commissioner within 60 days of the June 1 audited report filing.
Line up each CPA-raised matter against the internal audit deficiency log and mark it as already identified, newly identified, or disputed.
For newly identified matters ask why internal testing did not catch them and record the coverage gap as a scoping issue for next year's matrix.
Draft management's written response to each CPA matter stating the corrective action and completion date, as required for the Section 11 filing.
Route the combined package to the Chief Financial Officer and the Audit Committee before it is filed.
checklist.done: every CPA-raised matter is reconciled to the internal deficiency log and has a dated management response ready for the Section 11 filing.

checklist.step: Report results to the Audit Committee and prepare the significant deficiency filing
actions: Prepare the Audit Committee pack: controls tested versus planned, pass rate, exceptions by process, graded deficiencies with remediation status, and the reconciliation to the CPA management letter.
State plainly whether any material weakness is unremediated at December 31, because that drives the conclusion in Management's Report of ICFR.

Where a significant deficiency remains unremediated, prepare the report describing the deficiency and the remediation plan for filing with the domiciliary commissioner alongside management's response, and hand it to the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Post the pack to the board portal at least 5 business days before the meeting and record the minute reference once tabled.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee has received a dated pack with pass rates and graded deficiencies, and any unremediated significant deficiency has a drafted filing ready.

testing.step: Build the population of planned versus executed control tests
actions: Export from AuditBoard the approved test plan (control id, risk rank, assigned auditor, planned timing) and the executed test log for the statutory year.
Build one row per planned control showing planned timing, actual completion date, sample size planned and tested, and the recorded conclusion.
Add the frozen key control export as a third source so controls that were never planned at all become visible.
Sign the population as complete and record the export timestamps for all three sources.
testing.done: the population shows every key control against its planned test and its executed test, from three reconciled sources.

testing.step: Reconcile the executed tests to the frozen ICFR matrix
actions: Match every key control in the frozen matrix to an executed test on control id and statutory year.
List unmatched key controls as untested-control exceptions and confirm whether the CPA tested them under the reliance agreement instead.
Confirm every executed test maps to a control still in the frozen matrix — tests on removed controls indicate the matrix change did not reach the plan.
Resolve every difference with the Chief Audit Executive before drawing the sample.
testing.done: every frozen key control is matched to an executed internal or CPA test, or listed as an untested-control exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of completed test workpapers
actions: Take 100% of controls graded HIGH risk, all controls where an exception was raised, and all controls that were remediated and retested.
Take a seeded random sample of 25 of the remaining completed tests, spread so no single auditor contributes more than a third.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and draw date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Add any control tested by an auditor who previously worked in that process as a mandatory sample row for independence review.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from a recorded seed and covers all high-risk, exception and remediated controls.

testing.step: Re-perform the test on a sampled control without reading the original conclusion
actions: For 10 sampled controls open the test program and evidence but not the conclusion, and re-test the same attributes on the same items.
Reach your own pass or deviation call per attribute, then compare to the original — a difference is an exception, including a right conclusion reached on the wrong attribute.
Re-draw the sample from the recorded seed and population to confirm the tested items are genuinely the ones the seed produces.
Capture your re-performance notes and the compared conclusions into the review workpaper.
testing.done: each re-performed control has an independent attribute-level conclusion and a documented comparison to the original.

testing.step: Verify sample sizes and population sources against the methodology
actions: For each sampled test compare the tested sample size to the methodology table for that control's frequency and risk rank.
Confirm the population source is a named report with recorded parameters, and re-run it to confirm the population count the sample was drawn from.
Confirm any sample below the table minimum carries written Chief Audit Executive approval dated before testing, not after.
Flag any test whose population came from a spreadsheet handed over by the control owner with no system trace.
testing.done: every sampled test has a table-compliant size, a reproducible population count and written approval for any shortfall.

testing.step: Trace evidence for sampled exceptions back to source records
actions: For each sampled exception open the underlying source record — the journal entry, the reconciliation, the access request ticket, the change record — and confirm the failure as described.
Confirm the exception form names the sampled item id, the attribute failed and the account and assertion affected, not just the control id.
Confirm the control owner's written factual confirmation is on file and predates the grading date.
Any exception that cannot be traced to a source record is itself an exception against the testing process.
testing.done: every sampled exception traces to a source record and carries an owner-confirmed, item-level description.

testing.step: Recompute the deviation rates, severity grades and remediation timing maths
actions: Recompute deviation rate = deviations divided by items tested for each sampled control and compare to the recorded rate.
Recompute whether the first-deviation sample extension actually doubled the original size, and whether a second deviation correctly failed the control.
Recompute the maximum potential misstatement against statutory materiality and capital and surplus and test whether the assigned grade follows the rubric.
Recompute the remediation window: go-live date plus at least 30 days of operation must fall on or before December 31, and confirm retests used only post-go-live occurrences.
testing.done: deviation rates, extension logic, severity grades and the 30-day remediation window all recompute to the recorded values.

testing.step: Test the reconciliation to the CPA management letter and the Section 11 package
actions: Obtain the CPA's written communication of internal control related matters and confirm every matter in it appears on the reconciliation with a status of already identified, newly identified or disputed.
Confirm each matter has a dated management response naming a corrective action and completion date, ready for filing within 60 days of the June 1 audited report.
Confirm every newly identified matter generated a scoping issue for the following year's matrix.
Confirm any unremediated significant deficiency has a drafted report describing the deficiency and remediation plan ready for the domiciliary commissioner.
testing.done: the CPA management letter reconciles item-for-item to the deficiency log with dated management responses and a drafted filing where required.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracked issue per testing exception naming the control id, the sampled test, what failed in the testing process and its effect on the year's conclusion.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list — control never planned, sample undersized, population unsourced, evidence not retained, retest before go-live, independence breach — and an owner in Internal Audit.
Set a remediation date ahead of the next planning cycle so the methodology or plan is corrected before the following year's testing starts.
Carry every open exception into the following year's test plan as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every testing exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an Internal Audit owner, a remediation date and a carry-forward retest.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the Audit Committee
actions: Compute coverage (key controls tested divided by key controls in the frozen matrix) and the workpaper exception rate, and compare both to the zero-untested-control threshold.
Write the conclusion — testing effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references and naming any control the conclusion could not cover.
Have the independent reviewer, who performed none of the sampled tests and has never operated a tested control, sign the review workpaper with name and date.
Table the conclusion, the deficiency status and the reconciliation to the CPA letter at the next Audit Committee meeting through the board portal and record the minute reference.
testing.done: a signed review workpaper states a conclusion, coverage and exception rates, and the Audit Committee minute reference where it was reported.
