checklist.step: Confirm the Audit Committee meets the Section 14 composition requirement for the group's premium volume
actions: Compute prior-year direct plus assumed written premium for the group from the filed Annual Statements and place it against the Section 14 bands: no independence requirement below $300 million, a majority independent between $300 million and $500 million, and 75% independent above $500 million.

Test each committee member against the Model 205 independence definition — no employment or compensatory relationship with the insurer or an affiliate other than board fees — and record the basis per member.
Where the group relies on the parent's audit committee acting for the insurer subsidiaries, confirm the domiciliary state permits it and record the citation.
Update the committee composition schedule in the board portal with each member's independence status and the date it was assessed.
Raise any shortfall to the Board chair before the audit engagement is approved.
checklist.done: the composition schedule shows the computed premium band, each member's independence basis and a compliant percentage, dated for the engagement year.

checklist.step: Test the proposed CPA firm against the Section 7 qualification requirements
actions: Obtain from the firm written confirmation that it is a member in good standing of the AICPA, that the engagement partners are licensed in the states where required, and that it is in good standing with the domiciliary state board of accountancy.
Check the firm and the named partners against the domiciliary commissioner's list of accountants found not qualified or disqualified under Section 7.
Confirm the firm conforms to AICPA and SEC independence standards and to the applicable rules of the domiciliary state's board of accountancy.
Obtain the firm's most recent peer review report and read the opinion and any letter of comments.
File the confirmations and the peer review report in the compliance evidence repository under the engagement year.
checklist.done: written AICPA good-standing, licensing, disqualification-check and peer review evidence is on file before the engagement letter is signed.

checklist.step: Register the appointed accountant with the domiciliary commissioner
actions: Prepare the written notice naming the accounting firm, the engagement partner, the insurer and its NAIC company code, and the audit years covered.

File the notice with the Alaska Division of Insurance and each other domiciliary commissioner within 60 days of the insurer becoming subject to the regulation, and again within the required window on any change of accountant.

Attach the statement, signed by the accountant, that the accountant is aware of the provisions of the insurance code and the accounting and financial reporting regulations of the state and will express an opinion on the statutory financial statements in terms of conformity with statutory accounting practices — the awareness letter.
Record the filing date, method and the recipient's acknowledgement on the regulatory calendar for each jurisdiction.
Diary the next required notification date.
checklist.done: each domiciliary commissioner has an on-file accountant registration with an attached awareness letter and a recorded acknowledgement.

checklist.step: Obtain and check the Accountant's Letter of Qualifications
actions: Request the Section 9 Letter of Qualifications from the engagement partner ahead of the June 1 audited report filing so it can be filed with the report.

Confirm the letter states the firm is independent with respect to the insurer and conforms to the standards of its profession, sets out the background and experience of the principal and staff assigned, and confirms the firm understands the audited statutory report and its opinion will be filed with the commissioner.

Confirm it states the accountant consents to the commissioner's review of the workpapers and to photocopies being made, and that it addresses any determination previously made that the accountant is not qualified.
Return the letter to the firm for correction where any of these elements is missing rather than filing an incomplete letter.
File the accepted letter with the audited report package and store the signed copy in the financial reporting repository.
checklist.done: a signed Letter of Qualifications containing every Section 9 element is on file and attached to the June 1 filing package.

checklist.step: Maintain the lead and concurring partner rotation register
actions: Record for the insurer each year: the lead (coordinating) audit partner, the concurring or engagement quality review partner, and the first year each served in that role.

Compute consecutive years served and flag any partner reaching five consecutive years — Section 7 bars the same lead or concurring partner from acting for more than five consecutive years and imposes a five-year cooling-off before returning.
Confirm with the firm in writing the successor partner's name at least 12 months before the rotation year so transition planning does not become a compliance argument.
Where the insurer seeks the Section 7 relief available to small insurers on hardship grounds, record the application to the domiciliary commissioner and the written determination received.
Update the register at each engagement approval and file the version in the board portal.
checklist.done: the register shows years served for both partners with no one past five consecutive years, or a documented commissioner relief determination on file.

checklist.step: Screen the engagement against the prohibited non-audit services list
actions: Take the Section 7G prohibited list: bookkeeping or other services related to the accounting records or financial statements, financial information systems design and implementation, appraisal or valuation services and fairness opinions, actuarially-oriented advisory services involving amounts recorded in the financial statements, internal audit outsourcing, management or human resources functions, broker-dealer or investment adviser services, legal or expert services unrelated to the audit.
Set the audit firm and its network firms as restricted suppliers in Coupa / SAP Ariba so any requisition naming them routes to the Corporate Secretary before a purchase order is issued.
Test each requested service against the list and reject prohibited services outright — pre-approval cannot cure a prohibited service.
Where an actuarial or valuation service is requested, confirm with the Appointed Actuary whether the amounts feed the statutory financial statements before deciding.
Log every rejection with the requester and the basis.
checklist.done: the audit firm is a gated supplier and every requested service has a recorded prohibited/permissible determination against the Section 7G list.

checklist.step: Run the Audit Committee pre-approval process for permissible non-audit services
actions: Require every permissible non-audit service to be pre-approved by the Audit Committee before the work starts, with the service description, scope, estimated fee and the reason the audit firm is the right provider.
Where pre-approval is delegated to the committee chair between meetings, confirm the delegation is in the charter and that the chair reports each approval to the full committee at its next meeting.

Record the de minimis exception conditions where relied on: the aggregate of such services is not more than 5% of total amounts paid to the accountant in the fiscal year, the service was not recognised as non-audit at engagement time, and it is promptly brought to and approved by the committee before the audit completes.
Track actual fees against the approved estimate and require re-approval on any overrun above the approved amount.
Minute every approval with the date, the service and the fee cap in the board portal.
checklist.done: every non-audit service has a dated pre-approval or a fully documented de minimis approval, with fees tracked against the cap.

checklist.step: Confirm the partner compensation prohibition with the firm
actions: Obtain the firm's written confirmation that the lead audit partner is not compensated, directly or indirectly, based on selling to the insurer services other than audit, review and attest services.
Ask the engagement partner to confirm the confirmation covers the network firms serving the group, not only the signing office.
Record the confirmation date against the engagement year in the independence file and require a fresh confirmation each engagement.
Raise any qualified or hedged confirmation to the Audit Committee chair before the engagement letter is signed.
checklist.done: a written, unqualified partner compensation confirmation covering the network firms is on file for the engagement year.

checklist.step: Screen hires into financial reporting oversight roles for the cooling-off period
actions: Define the covered roles in the HRIS: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, Controller, Chief Accounting Officer, and any role with direct responsibility for the statutory financial statements.

Add a mandatory pre-offer question and a background screen asking whether the candidate participated in the audit of the insurer as a member of the audit firm's engagement team within the one year preceding the start of the audit year.

Route any positive answer to the Corporate Secretary and General Counsel for a written determination before an offer is extended — Section 7 bars the insurer from accepting an audit where such a person has been hired within that period.
Record the screen result on the requisition so the evidence sits with the hire, not in an email thread.
Report screened hires into covered roles to the Audit Committee annually.
checklist.done: every hire into a covered role has a recorded cooling-off screen result and, where positive, a written General Counsel determination before offer.

checklist.step: Obtain the annual written independence communication before fieldwork
actions: Request the firm's annual written communication describing all relationships between the firm, its network firms and the insurer and its affiliates that may reasonably bear on independence.
Confirm the letter includes the firm's affirmation that it is independent under the applicable AICPA and state board rules and, where relevant, the SEC and PCAOB standards.
Discuss the disclosed relationships with the firm at the Audit Committee meeting and minute the committee's conclusion on independence.
Confirm the letter is dated before fieldwork begins; a letter dated after the audit report is evidence of nothing.
File the letter and the minute extract in the board portal independence file.
checklist.done: a pre-fieldwork independence letter is on file and the Audit Committee's independence conclusion is minuted.

checklist.step: Track fees by category and reconcile them to the pre-approval register
actions: Set up distinct GL accounts or cost codes for audit fees, audit-related fees, tax fees and all other fees paid to the audit firm and its network firms.
Each quarter extract every invoice paid to the firm from accounts payable, including invoices posted by subsidiaries and by non-finance cost centres.
Reconcile each invoice to a pre-approval reference; anything unmatched goes to the Corporate Secretary the same week for a de minimis assessment or an exception.
Compute the running non-audit-to-total fee ratio so the 5% de minimis condition can be tested at any point in the year.
Report the fee schedule by category to the Audit Committee at each meeting.
checklist.done: every invoice paid to the audit firm ties to a pre-approval reference and the non-audit fee ratio is computed and reported quarterly.

checklist.step: Run the dismissal, resignation and disagreement notification protocol
actions: Trigger the protocol the moment the accountant is dismissed or resigns, whichever is earlier, and start the 5-business-day clock.
Notify the domiciliary commissioner in writing within 5 business days that the accountant is no longer engaged, naming the insurer, the firm and the effective date.

Within the following 10 business days furnish the commissioner with the separate letter stating whether, in the 24 months preceding the event, there were any disagreements with the former accountant on accounting principles, auditing scope or procedure, or financial statement disclosure, describing each disagreement and whether it was resolved.
Request the former accountant's letter stating whether they agree with the insurer's statements, and forward it to the commissioner.
Log every date, recipient and acknowledgement against the event in the regulatory calendar.
checklist.done: the 5-business-day notification and the 10-business-day disagreements letter are filed with recorded dates and the accountant's concurrence letter is forwarded.

checklist.step: Take the engagement and the independence conclusion to the Audit Committee for approval
actions: Assemble the meeting pack: qualification evidence, rotation register, independence letter, prior-year fee schedule by category, the pre-approval register and the proposed engagement letter with scope and fee.
Post the pack to the board portal at least 5 business days before the meeting so members can read it.
Ask the committee to resolve on the record: appointment of the accountant, approval of the audit scope and fee, and its determination that the accountant is independent and qualified.
Minute the resolution with the date, the members present and any abstention, and have the chair approve the minutes at the following meeting.
Release the engagement letter for signature only after the resolution is minuted.
checklist.done: a minuted Audit Committee resolution appoints the accountant and records the independence and qualification determination before the engagement letter is signed.

checklist.step: Handle consolidated or group audit arrangements under Section 8
actions: Where an insurer is part of a group and a consolidated or combined audit is proposed, obtain the domiciliary commissioner's written permission before relying on it in place of a separate audit.

Prepare the columnar consolidating or combining worksheet showing amounts for each insurer separately, the non-insurance operations on a combined basis, explanations of consolidating and eliminating entries, and a reconciliation of the audited amounts to the amounts reported in each insurer's Annual Statement.
Confirm the same accountant covers all entities relied on and record any component auditor and the extent of reliance placed on them.
File the worksheet with the audited report and store the commissioner's permission letter alongside it.
checklist.done: any consolidated audit has written commissioner permission and a columnar worksheet reconciling each insurer to its Annual Statement.

checklist.step: Close, index and retain the engagement-year independence file
actions: Copy the complete file — qualification evidence, awareness letter, Letter of Qualifications, independence letter, partner compensation confirmation, rotation register version, pre-approval register, fee schedule, cooling-off screens and the appointing minutes — into the compliance evidence repository under the engagement year.
Index it by insurer, NAIC company code, engagement year and accounting firm so a commissioner request can be answered by entity.
Apply the 7-year retention label from the engagement year end and set deletion holds.
Spot-check retrieval of three items — the rotation register, one pre-approval resolution and the Letter of Qualifications — and record the test.
checklist.done: the engagement-year independence file is filed, indexed by insurer and year, retention-labelled and proven retrievable.

testing.step: Build the population of audit firm engagements, invoices and covered hires
actions: Extract from accounts payable every invoice paid in the engagement year to the audit firm and any entity sharing its name or network, across all legal entities and cost centres, not just the finance ledger.
Extract the pre-approval register from the board portal and the requisition history for the firm from Coupa / SAP Ariba.
Extract from the HRIS every hire and internal move into a covered financial reporting oversight role during the year.
Add the partner rotation register and the Audit Committee membership schedule as separate population sections.
Sign the population as complete and record each extract's timestamp and filter criteria.
testing.done: the population covers every firm invoice, every pre-approval, every covered hire, the rotation register and committee composition, signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the fee ledger to the pre-approval register
actions: Match every invoice to a pre-approval reference on service description and entity, and total fees by category — audit, audit-related, tax, other.
List invoices with no matching pre-approval and check whether a documented de minimis approval exists that met all three conditions.
Reconcile the total paid to the fee schedule reported to the Audit Committee and explain any difference.
Confirm no invoice exceeds its approved fee cap without a documented re-approval.
testing.done: every invoice matches a pre-approval or a complete de minimis approval, and totals tie to the schedule reported to the committee.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of engagements and approvals
actions: Take 100% of non-audit engagements, all invoices over the de minimis materiality, all covered-role hires and both partner rotation records.
Take a seeded random sample of 20 audit and audit-related invoices from the remainder.
Record the seed, population size and draw date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Add every engagement with a network firm outside the signing office as a mandatory sample row.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from a recorded seed and covers all non-audit engagements, covered hires and partner rotation records.

testing.step: Re-perform the prohibited-service determination on each sampled non-audit engagement
actions: Read the statement of work for each sampled non-audit engagement before opening the recorded determination.

Test it yourself against the Section 7G prohibited list, paying particular attention to actuarially-oriented advisory work, valuation and fairness opinions, internal audit outsourcing and systems implementation.
Compare your conclusion to the recorded one; a difference is an exception including where the right conclusion rests on the wrong prohibition category.
Where the service touches amounts recorded in the statutory financial statements, confirm with the Appointed Actuary or the Controller which balance it feeds and record that in the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled non-audit engagement has an independent prohibited/permissible conclusion documented and compared to the recorded determination.

testing.step: Recompute partner rotation years and the Section 14 composition percentage
actions: Recompute consecutive years served for the lead and concurring partner from the engagement letters and audit reports rather than from the register itself, and compare to the five-year limit.
Where a partner returned after rotating off, recompute the cooling-off years served away and test against the five-year requirement.

Recompute prior-year direct plus assumed written premium from the filed Annual Statements and re-derive the Section 14 band, then recompute the independent-member percentage from the membership schedule.
Any partner at or beyond five consecutive years without a documented commissioner relief determination, or any percentage below the band requirement, is a fail.
testing.done: rotation years, cooling-off years, the premium band and the independent-member percentage all recompute and satisfy the thresholds.

testing.step: Trace the Section 9 and awareness letters to the filed audit package
actions: Open the filed June 1 audited report package and confirm the Accountant's Letter of Qualifications and the awareness letter are physically in it, signed and dated.

Check the Letter of Qualifications against the Section 9 element list — independence affirmation, background and experience of principal and assigned staff, understanding that the report will be filed with the commissioner, consent to commissioner review and photocopying of workpapers, and any prior qualification determination.
Confirm the awareness letter is signed by the accountant and states awareness of the state's insurance code and accounting and financial reporting regulations.
A letter that is on file but missing an element is an exception, not a documentation nicety.
testing.done: both letters are present in the filed package, signed and dated, with every required element verified line by line.

testing.step: Test the notification timing maths on any accountant change
actions: Identify any dismissal, resignation or change of accountant in the year and establish the event date from the board minutes or the firm's letter, whichever is earlier.
Recompute the 5-business-day notification deadline and the 10-business-day disagreements-letter deadline from that date using the state's business day convention.
Compare the recomputed deadlines to the actual filing dates and acknowledgements on the regulatory calendar and treat any overrun as a reportable breach.
Confirm the disagreements letter covers the full 24-month look-back and that the former accountant's concurrence letter was obtained and forwarded.
testing.done: every accountant change has recomputed deadlines met on the evidence, a 24-month disagreements look-back and a forwarded concurrence letter.

testing.step: Test the cooling-off screening on covered-role hires
actions: For each covered-role hire in the population, open the requisition and confirm the cooling-off question was asked and answered before the offer date, not after.
For any positive answer confirm a dated written General Counsel determination exists and predates the offer.
Independently check the named individuals against the audit firm's engagement team lists for the prior audit year where the firm will provide them.
Any covered-role hire with no recorded screen is an exception even where the individual demonstrably never worked on the audit.
testing.done: every covered-role hire has a pre-offer screen result and every positive answer has a pre-offer General Counsel determination.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracked issue per exception naming the engagement or individual, the Section 7, 9 or 14 requirement breached and the fee or period involved.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — supplier gate bypassed, delegated approval unreported, rotation register not updated, screen skipped, notification clock missed — and an owner.

Set a remediation date and, for a prohibited service or a rotation breach, open an impact assessment with General Counsel on whether the audit opinion itself is affected and whether the commissioner must be told.
Report every exception to the Audit Committee at its next meeting regardless of size and carry it into next year's test as a mandatory row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, where independence is impaired, a General Counsel impact assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the Audit Committee
actions: Compute the exception count against the zero-tolerance threshold for prohibited services, un-pre-approved engagements, rotation breaches and cooling-off breaches.
Write the conclusion — independence supported, supported with exceptions, or impaired — citing the workpaper references and naming any engagement the conclusion could not cover.
Have the independent reviewer, who has no role in engaging or paying the audit firm, sign the workpaper with name and date.
Table the conclusion at the Audit Committee meeting that re-appoints the accountant, record the minute reference, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states an independence conclusion with the exception count and the Audit Committee minute reference where it was reported.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Controller owns the annual audited statutory report filing and the auditor communications package; the Regulatory Reporting Manager executes the per-jurisdiction submissions and the Chief Financial Officer signs the Section 16 report

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Alaska AS 21.09.200 and 3 AAC 21 (Alaska's adoption of NAIC Model 205, Section 4 annual audited financial report due June 1) re-read each filing season, with the Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona adoptions and the remaining 47 jurisdictions checked for altered due dates, extension procedures and Section 11/16 adoption

In-scope processes.value: Annual statutory close and audit through to filing: preparation of the audited statutory financial statements for each insurer, reconciliation to the March 1 Annual Statement, the June 1 audited report filing in all 51 jurisdictions where licensed, the August 1 Section 11 communication of internal control related matters, and the Section 16 Management's Report of ICFR

In-scope systems.value: NAIC Financial Data Repository submissions via iSite+ plus each state's own filing channel; statements prepared from the statutory GL and the Annual Statement compiler, with the signed package held in the financial reporting repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Annual Audited Statutory Report Filing Procedure — jurisdiction calendar, package contents checklist, Annual Statement reconciliation, audit adjustment posting rules, extension request protocol, submission channel by state and proof-of-filing capture

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer each January before filing season opens and reviewed by the Audit Committee alongside the audit timetable; re-approved on any state change to due dates or submission channel

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual Statement March 1; audited statutory financial report June 1 in each of the 51 jurisdictions; communication of internal control related matters within 60 days of the audited report filing (August 1); Section 16 Management's Report of ICFR August 1; adverse financial condition notification within 5 business days of the accountant determining it; any extension request filed before June 1 in the form the state requires

Deadline reminders configured.value: Regulatory calendar milestones at T-60 (audit fieldwork complete), T-30 (draft statements to the CPA), T-14 (opinion expected), T-5 (package assembled) and T-0 June 1 per jurisdiction, each escalating to the Controller then the Chief Financial Officer if the task is still open

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Filed audited statements, accountant's opinion, awareness letter, Letter of Qualifications, Section 11 communication with management's response, Section 16 report, extension approvals and every submission confirmation retained 7 years from the statutory year end in the financial reporting repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any jurisdiction filed after June 1 without an approved extension, any missing package component and any unreconciled difference to the Annual Statement is logged as a filing exception with jurisdiction, days late, root cause and remediation

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CFO signs off every late or amended filing and the accompanying explanation to the commissioner; the Controller signs off package-completeness remediation

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every insurer-jurisdiction filing obligation for the statutory year — each licensed insurer across all 51 jurisdictions — plus the Section 11 and Section 16 filings and any extension requests and amended filings

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any jurisdiction not filed by June 1 without an approved extension, any package missing the opinion, awareness letter or Letter of Qualifications, or any unexplained difference between the audited statements and the filed Annual Statement is a fail and is escalated to the Chief Financial Officer and the Audit Committee

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; the test runs once per filing season in June covering the June 1 filings, with a follow-on August pass covering the Section 11 and Section 16 filings

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: An Internal Auditor who prepared no statement, performed no submission and owns no statutory close control

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual filing compliance workpaper — jurisdiction obligation list, submission confirmations, package completeness matrix, Annual Statement reconciliation and exceptions — filed in the compliance evidence repository under the statutory year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The complete filed package per jurisdiction with its submission confirmation, the Annual Statement reconciliation and any extension approval, producible to a Division of Insurance financial analyst within 5 business days of request

Regulator response path.value: The Statutory Reporting Manager is the single point of contact for Alaska Division of Insurance and lead-state analyst questions on the audited report; the Chief Financial Officer signs any explanation of a late or amended filing and General Counsel clears any adverse-condition communication

checklist.step: Build the filing obligation calendar across all 51 jurisdictions
actions: List every licensed insurer with its NAIC company code and its licence status in each of the 51 jurisdictions, taking the licence list from the state licence register rather than from memory.

For each insurer-jurisdiction pair record the audited report due date (June 1 baseline, per Alaska AS 21.09.200 and each state's adoption), the submission channel, whether the state has adopted Sections 11 and 16, and the extension procedure.
Mark jurisdictions where the state accepts the NAIC Financial Data Repository submission as satisfying the filing and those that additionally require a direct or paper copy.
Send the calendar to the Controller and the Statutory Reporting Manager by January 31 and load every due date into the regulatory calendar with owners.
Flag any insurer that qualifies for a Section 4 exemption and record the basis and the exemption request status.
checklist.done: every insurer-jurisdiction pair has a due date, a channel, Section 11/16 flags and a named owner loaded into the calendar.

checklist.step: Prepare the audited statutory financial statements for each insurer
actions: Build for each insurer the statutory-basis balance sheet, statement of operations, statement of changes in capital and surplus and statement of cash flow, with the prior year presented for comparison.

Draft the notes to the financial statements to the NAIC Annual Statement Instructions note set, giving particular attention to reserves, reinsurance, related party transactions, investments and subsequent events.
Confirm the statements are presented on the basis of accounting practices prescribed or permitted by the domiciliary state and disclose any permitted practice with its surplus effect.
Route the draft to the Controller for review and then to the engagement partner on the date agreed in the audit timetable.
Version each draft so the change from draft to opinion-ready is traceable.
checklist.done: each insurer has a complete, versioned draft statutory financial statement set with notes, on the domiciliary basis, delivered to the CPA on the timetable date.

checklist.step: Reconcile the audited statements to the filed Annual Statement
actions: Take the Annual Statement filed by March 1 and tie the audited balance sheet to Page 2 and Page 3 and the audited operations statement to Page 4, line by line.
Tie capital and surplus to Page 4 the Capital and Surplus Account and to the Five-Year Historical Data page.
Build the reconciliation schedule showing each difference with its cause: audit adjustment, reclassification, or an error requiring an amended Annual Statement.
Where a difference exceeds the audit adjustment threshold agreed with the CPA, escalate to the Controller the same day.
Have the Controller sign the reconciliation before the package is assembled.
checklist.done: a signed reconciliation ties audited surplus and net income to the filed Annual Statement with every difference explained.

checklist.step: Clear audit adjustments and decide whether the Annual Statement must be amended
actions: Take the CPA's summary of adjustments — both posted and passed — and record each with its surplus and net income effect.
Post the accepted adjustments to the statutory GL in the correct statutory year and confirm the trial balance re-extracts to the audited figures.
Assess the passed adjustments in aggregate against statutory materiality and document why they remain unposted.
Decide with the Statutory Reporting Manager whether an amended Annual Statement must be filed and, if so, file it and note the amendment on the reconciliation.
Notify the Appointed Actuary where an adjustment touches loss reserves so the actuarial opinion and Schedule P remain consistent.
checklist.done: all accepted adjustments are posted, passed adjustments are assessed against materiality, and the amended-Annual-Statement decision is documented.

checklist.step: Obtain the accountant's report and confirm its dating and addressing
actions: Obtain the signed accountant's report expressing an opinion on the statutory financial statements in terms of their conformity with statutory accounting practices prescribed or permitted by the domiciliary state.
Confirm the opinion type (unmodified, qualified, adverse, disclaimer) and, where anything other than unmodified, brief the Chief Financial Officer and the Audit Committee chair immediately.
Check the report names the correct insurer and NAIC company code, covers the correct periods, and is dated no earlier than the date sufficient audit evidence was obtained.
Obtain the signed management representation letter dated the same day as the opinion.
Store the signed opinion in the financial reporting repository under the insurer and statutory year.
checklist.done: a signed, correctly dated accountant's report on the statutory basis exists for each insurer with a matching management representation letter.

checklist.step: Assemble the June 1 filing package per jurisdiction
actions: Build the package: accountant's report, audited statutory financial statements with notes, the awareness letter, the Accountant's Letter of Qualifications, and any state-specific transmittal or cover form.
Run the completeness matrix — one row per insurer-jurisdiction, one column per required component — and refuse to release any package with a blank cell.
Confirm each PDF is text-searchable, correctly paginated, under the portal file size limit and named to the state's convention (<NAIC code>_<year>_AuditedFinancialReport.pdf as the working standard).
Have the Controller review and release the package for submission.
Lock the released version so what is filed and what is retained are provably the same file.
checklist.done: every insurer-jurisdiction package is complete on the matrix, correctly named, and released by the Controller as a locked version.

checklist.step: Prepare and route the Section 16 Management's Report of ICFR for filing
actions: Confirm from the premium threshold test which insurers exceed $500 million direct plus assumed written premium and therefore owe the Section 16 report.

Take the signed report from the Chief Financial Officer and confirm it names COSO 2013 as the framework, states the December 31 assessment date and gives a clear conclusion with any unremediated material weakness described.
Confirm each jurisdiction's adoption row to establish where the report is due and note that it is due within 60 days of the audited report filing — August 1 on the June 1 baseline.
Where an insurer relies on a group-level report, confirm the domiciliary state accepts it and record the citation.
Hand the report and the jurisdiction list to the Regulatory Reporting Manager with the August 1 deadline set.
checklist.done: the signed Section 16 report is matched to the jurisdictions that require it, with the August 1 deadline loaded and any group-level reliance documented.

checklist.step: Request an extension where the June 1 date cannot be met
actions: Trigger the extension protocol the moment the audit timetable shows the opinion will not be signed with 10 days to spare before June 1.
Write to the domiciliary commissioner before June 1 stating the insurer, NAIC code, the reason for the delay, the work outstanding and the requested revised date, and copy the engagement partner.
Follow each state's own extension form or procedure where one exists rather than a generic letter, and confirm whether the state requires the accountant to write separately.
Record the request date, the commissioner's response and the granted date on the regulatory calendar, and treat a request with no response as not granted.
Brief the Chief Financial Officer and the Audit Committee chair on every extension sought.
checklist.done: every extension is requested in writing before June 1 in the state's own form, with the granted date recorded — or the filing is made on time.

checklist.step: Submit through the NAIC Financial Data Repository
actions: Log in to NAIC iSite+ with the company's filing credentials and open the Financial Data Repository filing area for the statutory year.
Select the insurer by NAIC company code, choose the audited financial report filing type and upload the released PDF package.
Confirm the jurisdiction distribution list the repository will serve and add any state the group is licensed in that is not pre-populated.
Submit and download the submission confirmation showing the company code, filing type, timestamp and jurisdictions served.
Attach the confirmation to the completeness matrix row for every jurisdiction it covers.
checklist.done: each insurer's package is uploaded and submitted with a downloaded confirmation naming the timestamp and the jurisdictions served.

checklist.step: File directly with states that require their own channel
actions: Work the calendar rows flagged as direct-filing states and open each state's own portal, secure email address or paper filing address as recorded.
Complete the state's transmittal or cover form with the insurer name, NAIC code, statutory year and the components enclosed, and pay any filing fee by the method the state accepts.
For the Alaska Division of Insurance submit the audited report to the Division's designated filing channel before June 1 and capture the acknowledgement.
Where a state requires a hard copy, send it by a trackable method and file the dispatch receipt and delivery proof.
Update the calendar row to FILED with the date, channel and reference.
checklist.done: every direct-filing jurisdiction is filed through its own channel before June 1 with a captured acknowledgement or delivery proof.

checklist.step: Capture and verify proof of filing for every jurisdiction
actions: For each insurer-jurisdiction row attach the submission confirmation, acknowledgement email or delivery proof and record the filing timestamp.
Compare the filing timestamp to the recorded due date and mark ON TIME, LATE or EXTENSION-COVERED; do not leave a row unmarked.
Where a repository submission was intended to serve a state, verify against that state's own filing record or contact the state to confirm receipt rather than assuming distribution worked.
Escalate every LATE row to the Controller within one business day with the reason and the proposed communication to the commissioner.
Close the season only when every row carries a proof and a timing status.
checklist.done: every insurer-jurisdiction row carries a filing proof, a timestamp and an on-time/late/extension status, with lates escalated.

checklist.step: File the communication of internal control related matters by August 1
actions: Obtain the accountant's written communication of any unremediated material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting noted during the audit; where none were noted, obtain the accountant's written statement to that effect.
Prepare management's written description of remedial actions taken or proposed for each matter raised, with owners and completion dates.
Confirm the filing deadline of 60 days after the audited report was filed — August 1 on the June 1 baseline — per each jurisdiction's adoption row.
Route the combined communication and response to the Chief Financial Officer and the Audit Committee before it is filed.
Hand it to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for submission through the same channels used for the audited report and capture the confirmations.
checklist.done: the accountant's communication (or nil statement) plus management's remedial response is filed in every adopting jurisdiction within 60 days of the audited report, with confirmations captured.

checklist.step: File the unremediated significant deficiency report where one remains open
actions: Take the deficiency log from the Chief Audit Executive and identify any significant deficiency or material weakness unremediated at the reporting date.
Draft the report describing each deficiency, its effect on the statutory financial statements, the remediation plan and the target completion date, and have the Chief Financial Officer sign it.
Confirm which jurisdictions require the report and file it with the domiciliary commissioner alongside the Section 11 package.
Log the filing in the tracker with the jurisdiction, date and confirmation, and set a follow-up task to report completion of the remediation to the commissioner.
checklist.done: every unremediated significant deficiency is described in a signed report, filed where required, and tracked to remediation completion.

checklist.step: Run the 5-business-day adverse financial condition notification path
actions: Brief the engagement partner at the start of the audit on the obligation to notify the board and the commissioner where the accountant determines the insurer has materially misstated its financial condition or does not meet the minimum capital and surplus requirement.
On any such determination, notify the board of directors or its audit committee in writing the same day and start the 5-business-day clock for the commissioner notification.
Have General Counsel clear the wording, then file the notification with the domiciliary commissioner within 5 business days of the accountant's determination and record the date and acknowledgement.
Convene the Audit Committee within the same week to record the board's response and any capital action.
Log the event, the dates and the outcome in the regulatory calendar.
checklist.done: any adverse-condition determination has a same-day board notification, a commissioner notification inside 5 business days and a minuted committee response.

checklist.step: Close, index and retain the filing season evidence pack
actions: Copy into the compliance evidence repository the released package per insurer, the completeness matrix, the Annual Statement reconciliation, every submission confirmation, extension approvals, the Section 11 package and the Section 16 report.
Index by insurer, NAIC company code, jurisdiction and statutory year so an examiner asking about one state can be answered without opening the whole season.
Apply the 7-year retention label measured from the statutory year end and set deletion holds.
Run a retrieval test on three jurisdictions, confirming the filed package and its confirmation open together, and record the test result.
checklist.done: the season pack is filed, indexed by insurer and jurisdiction, retention-labelled and proven retrievable by a documented spot test.

testing.step: Build the population of insurer-jurisdiction filing obligations
actions: Extract every licensed insurer with its NAIC company code and the jurisdictions where it holds a certificate of authority from the licence register, not from the filing calendar being tested.
Build one population row per insurer-jurisdiction pair, adding the Section 11 and Section 16 obligations as separate rows where the jurisdiction adopted them.
Add any insurer claiming a Section 4 exemption as its own row so the exemption itself gets tested rather than silently removing the obligation.
Sign the population as complete and record the licence register extract date and filters.
testing.done: the population is a signed list of every insurer-jurisdiction obligation built from the licence register, including exemption claims.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the filing calendar and the submission log
actions: Match each population row to a calendar row and a submission log entry on insurer, NAIC code and jurisdiction.
List calendar rows with no population match (obligations invented) and population rows with no calendar match (obligations missed) — the second category is the dangerous one.
Confirm the recorded due date on each matched row against the jurisdiction's own adoption citation rather than the calendar's stated date.
Resolve every difference with the Regulatory Reporting Manager before drawing the sample.
testing.done: every obligation reconciles to a calendar row with a citation-verified due date, and unmatched rows are escalated.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of filings for tracing
actions: Take 100% of domiciliary state filings, every Section 16 filing, every extension-covered row and every row marked LATE.
Take a seeded random sample of 25 remaining insurer-jurisdiction rows spread so no single insurer contributes more than a third.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and draw date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Add every direct-filing jurisdiction as a mandatory sample row because those depend on manual submission rather than repository distribution.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from a recorded seed and covers all domiciliary, Section 16, extension, late and direct-filing rows.

testing.step: Trace each sampled filing to a regulator-side submission record
actions: For NAIC-channel rows open iSite+ and locate the submission by company code, filing type and statutory year, and read the submitted timestamp and the jurisdictions served.
For direct-filing rows open the state acknowledgement, portal receipt or courier delivery proof and confirm it names the insurer and the statutory year.
Compare the file that was submitted to the released locked version in the repository — same file, same page count, same opinion date.
A row with an internal 'filed' status but no regulator-side or carrier-side proof is an exception, not a records gap.
testing.done: every sampled row traces to a regulator-side or delivery proof naming the insurer, and the submitted file matches the released version.

testing.step: Test package completeness component by component
actions: Open each sampled submitted package and confirm it contains the accountant's report, the audited statutory statements with notes, the awareness letter and the Accountant's Letter of Qualifications, plus any state transmittal.
Confirm the accountant's report names the correct insurer and NAIC code, covers the right periods, expresses the opinion on the statutory basis of the domiciliary state, and is signed and dated.
Confirm any permitted or prescribed practice is disclosed in the notes with its surplus effect.
Score the package against the completeness matrix and treat any component present in the matrix but absent from the submitted file as a fail.
testing.done: every sampled package is verified component by component against the submitted file, not against the internal matrix alone.

testing.step: Re-perform the Annual Statement reconciliation on a sample of insurers
actions: For five sampled insurers take the filed Annual Statement and the audited statements and independently tie capital and surplus, net income and total admitted assets.
Reach your own difference list before opening the prepared reconciliation, then compare — an unexplained difference the reconciliation did not carry is an exception.
Confirm each posted audit adjustment traces to a journal entry in the statutory GL in the correct year and that passed adjustments are documented against materiality.
Where an amended Annual Statement was required, confirm it was actually filed and locate its submission confirmation.
testing.done: surplus, net income and admitted assets independently tie for each re-performed insurer, with every difference explained and any amendment proven filed.

testing.step: Recompute the filing deadline maths per jurisdiction
actions: Recompute the audited report due date from each sampled jurisdiction's adoption citation (June 1 baseline) and compare to the calendar's recorded date.
Recompute the Section 11 deadline as 60 days after the actual audited report filing date, not 60 days after June 1, and compare to the date filed.
Recompute days late for every LATE row using the state's own convention and confirm an approved extension covers any row marked extension-covered — a request with no response is not an extension.
Recompute the Section 16 premium threshold per insurer from the Annual Statement State Page and Schedule F to confirm the report was owed everywhere it was filed and filed everywhere it was owed.
testing.done: every sampled due date, the 60-day Section 11 clock, days-late counts and the Section 16 threshold recompute and agree with the recorded values.

testing.step: Test the Section 11 package and any adverse-condition notification
actions: Confirm the accountant's communication of unremediated material weaknesses — or the written nil statement — exists for each insurer and was filed in every adopting jurisdiction.
Confirm management's written remedial response names an action, an owner and a completion date for each matter raised, and that it went to the Audit Committee before filing.

Where any adverse financial condition determination occurred, recompute the 5-business-day clock from the accountant's determination date and confirm the board notification and the commissioner notification dates.
Confirm any unremediated significant deficiency report was signed by the Chief Financial Officer and filed where required.
testing.done: the Section 11 package, remedial responses and any adverse-condition notifications are verified present, timely and committee-reviewed.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the insurer, the jurisdiction, the component or deadline missed and the days late.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list — licence not on the calendar, repository distribution assumed, package component missing, opinion late from the CPA, extension requested but never granted — and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any missed filing, prepare the late filing with a written explanation for the commissioner signed by the Chief Financial Officer.
Carry every open exception into next season's test as a mandatory row and update the filing calendar so the same jurisdiction cannot be missed twice.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, for missed filings, a CFO-signed explanation to the commissioner.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the Audit Committee
actions: Compute the on-time filing rate and the package completeness rate across the population and compare both to the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion — filing obligations met, met with exceptions, or not met — naming each jurisdiction filed late or incompletely and citing the workpaper reference for each.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared no statement and executed no submission, sign the workpaper with name and date.

Table the conclusion, the late-filing list and the remediation plan at the next Audit Committee meeting through the board portal, record the minute reference and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states a conclusion with on-time and completeness rates and the Audit Committee minute reference where it was reported.
